Who is she? - The girl from the B12 department. - Oh, yes! But are you sure? - Not really, but I can ask her. Oh, by the way, is this yours? - WOW! That is my iPad - Joe’s kid found it. Here you have. - Thanks, Tom. See you later.

originalSource.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE A SMOKING GUN Something that is obvious; an indisputable truth You should have seen the smoking gun; that man could not be trusted. HIDDEN AGENDA Something that may refer to a secret plan or an implication I would not have expected Freddy to have a hidden agenda. A SHOT IN THE DARK To have an ide or suspicion about someone or something Thank God I had already gotten a shot in the dark about Tim, he almost got away with that. NUTS AND BOLTS The detailed information about someone or something and how it works If it had been me, I would have gone nut and bolts with Jenny; now she’s gone! AN INSIDE STORY Considered as an advice or a hot tip What an inside story John has just dropped us. A STRAW IN THE WIND It refers to an indication or sign that one can see or get from someone or something We should have seen the straw in the wind; now, we can’t do anything. UPPER HAND It means someone or something has a position of advantage and control Fortunately, I had already upper-handed the rest of the contestants. TIP OF THE ICEBERG The small piece or amount of something that we can see Handing over the project was just the tip of the iceberg.

Something that is obvious; an indisputable truth.
You should have seen the smoking gun; that man could not be trusted.
HIDDEN AGENDA
Something that may refer to a secret plan or an implication.
I would not have expected Freddy to have a hidden agenda.
A SHOT IN THE DARK
To have an ide or suspicion about someone or something.
Thank God I had already gotten a shot in the dark about Tim, he almost got away with that.
NUTS AND BOLTS
The detailed information about someone or something and how it works.
If it had been me, I would have gone nut and bolts with Jenny; now she’s gone!
AN INSIDE STORY
Considered as an advice or a hot tip.
What an inside story John has just dropped us.
A STRAW IN THE WIND
It refers to an indication or sign that one can see or get from someone or something.
We should have seen the straw in the wind; now, we can’t do anything.
UPPER HAND
It means someone or something has a position of advantage and control.
Fortunately, I had already upper-handed the rest of the contestants.
TIP OF THE ICEBERG
The small piece or amount of something that we can see.
Handing over the project was just the tip of the iceberg.
Look at the phrases and discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?
